basis: The state incidence map uses a color scale where darker red indicates higher incidence, with 0 (Low) at the bottom of the scale and 100 (High) at the top. Utah (UT) is colored dark burgundy, matching the 0 end of the scale. West Virginia (WV) is colored pale-yellow, matching the 100 end of the scale. Alabama (AL) is not visible on the map, as its polygon is gray and unlabeled, indicating no mapped incidence value. According to the public task rules, gray indicates an unmapped/missing category and is not eligible to exceed a mapped state. Therefore, among the three eligible options, West Virginia (WV) has the highest incidence.
